context: Weekly Market Metrics (#Week 44 (27 Oct–31 Oct, 2025) | What to expect next week
text: Hello and welcome to Weekly Market Metrics! We’re in week 44 of the year—just eight weeks left in 2025! Just the right time to plan your year-end holidays. Anyway, let me get back to business—time for our weekly dose of market metrics. This was a tepid week in the markets, nothing much exciting—markets are taking a breather of sorts. But this is also a month-end, and I have a lot to share. Outside markets, though, there were two exciting events: one was Trump meeting Xi in South Korea, and the tariff rationalization that was announced can be called a temporary de-escalation, but Indian markets don’t seem to be happy with it. And yes, I cannot miss mentioning India’s historic victory over Australia in the ICC Women’s World Cup semi-finals. That was something. Anyways, let’s get started with the charts and indexes. Nifty first. NIFTY 50 - Technical Analysis Monthly Timeframe With October over, let’s look at the monthly charts. Starting with NIFTY—in absolute terms, it added 1,111 points this month—a quadruple Nelson! Let’s hope the superstition doesn’t play out this time. I see a cup and handle forming on the monthly charts. What do you see? Maybe a saucer of chai getting ready for a breakout sip? But jokes aside, it really does look like a classic cup base—if the handle forms cleanly, this could turn out to be a kadak “chai pattern” of the year for NIFTY! Weekly Timeframe After breaking out of a 15-week consolidation, NIFTY is still hovering near that breakout zone around 25,700. It’s been two straight weeks where the index failed to close above the psychological 26,000 mark. Last week’s bearish doji turned out to be a solid warning. NIFTY tried to move above 26,100, the previous week’s high, but got rejected right at the same level again. For the week, the index slipped about 73 points, closing at 25,722, down roughly 0.28%. On the charts, immediate resistance remains at 26,100—that’s the high from the past two weeks—followed by the all-time high near 26,300. On the downside, support is steady at 25,700. So for now, NIFTY continues to move sideways between 25,700 and 26,100. My view—this looks more like a healthy pullback within the uptrend. If 25,700 holds, we could see another push higher in the coming weeks. Let’s see how the market plays it out. Daily Timeframe NIFTY opened strong on Monday, held gains through Wednesday, but Thursday and Friday erased the entire week’s progress. A doji on Tuesday’s monthly expiry hinted at indecision, and that played out as selling pressure near 26,100 in the latter half of the week. Resistance and support zones remain unchanged from the weekly chart—26,100 and 26,277 on the upside, and 25,670, followed by 25,450 as support. From the week’s high at 26,098, NIFTY slipped about 375 points—roughly a 1.44% decline—almost the same correction we saw last week. Hourly Timeframe NIFTY finally broke below the 50-EMA on Friday, the last trading day of October. Since 14th October, NIFTY has been trading above the 50-EMA, gaining about 740 points, or roughly 3%, and holding that level for nearly 17 calendar days—around 13 trading sessions. With the sell-off on Thursday and Friday, the price has now slipped about 110 points below the EMA. Historically, short trades don’t sustain well in NIFTY, and with the index near a critical support zone between 25,700 and 25,670, this will be the level to watch. Let’s see if bears finally hold—or get butchered like they usually do. Monthly Seasonality After a weak mid-year stretch, we’ve now had two consecutive green months, with October gaining 4.51%—the second-best month of the year after March’s +6.3%. In CY 2025, NIFTY has now logged 4 red months out of 10 this year with total gains of 8.79%. Historically, November and December have been strong months for NIFTY—with win rates of 60% and 68%, and average gains of 2.76% and 2.61%, respectively—the highest among all months. If the US deal goes through, it could act as the next big trigger, potentially pushing NIFTY beyond its all-time high. The data supports an upward bias—now it’s just about getting some catalyst to spark the rally. Overnight vs. Intraday Moves Both were negative this week. Even though NIFTY opened with positive gaps on Monday and Wednesday, the negative gaps on the other three days wiped out those gains. On an intraday basis, NIFTY slipped about -0.22% for the week. Looking at 2025 year-to-date, NIFTY has gained roughly +9.14% overnight, but only +0.92% intraday—showing that most of this year’s upside has actually come outside regular trading hours. BANK NIFTY - Technical Analysis Monthly Timeframe BANKNIFTY stood out with a strong 5.75% gain, adding nearly 3,140 points in October, and has given its highest-ever monthly close. Weekly Timeframe The last two weeks might look weak, but when you zoom out, the trend still looks firmly bullish. Essentially, it’s taking a breather near the highs, not reversing. If 57,600-57,400 hold as support, BANKNIFTY could be setting up for another leg higher once momentum kicks back in. This week’s candle was a spinning top, coming right after last week’s shooting star. Don’t get lost in the candlestick names—it simply means BANK NIFTY is facing resistance near the 58,500–58,600 zone. This week, the index made a high of 58,470 and reversed to close at 57,776, just 77 points higher, or about +0.13% for the week. After two weeks of almost no gains, the view remains bullish to sideways, with hopes that the 57,600 level holds as support. Resistance stays around 58,500–58,600. Daily Timeframe The resistance and support zones remain largely the same as on the weekly chart, with resistance around 58,600 and support between 57,600 and 57,400. BANK NIFTY printed three back-to-back green candles at the start of the week, followed by two red candles on Thursday and Friday, which erased most of the earlier gains. Hourly Timeframe Just like NIFTY, BANKNIFTY also broke below the 50-EMA and is now trading about 162 points, or roughly 0.3%, under it. It had stayed above the 50-EMA throughout October, maintaining steady momentum, and finally closed below it on the last trading day of the month. During this entire stretch, BANK NIFTY added nearly 3,100 points—marking its strongest monthly run since April—before cooling off toward the end of the month. NIFTY MIDCAP SELECT - Technical Analysis Monthly Timeframe MIDCPNIFTY logged its highest-ever monthly close, just like BANKNIFTY. The October high of 13,555 is the next key level to watch—once that’s crossed, MIDCPNIFTY enters blue-sky territory with no historical resistance overhead. For the month, it added 869 points, a solid 6.89% gain, making it one of the strongest performers on the index front. Weekly & Daily Timeframe Similar story for MIDCPNIFTY on the weekly and daily charts—resistance sits around 13,550, and support near 13,400. For the week, MIDCPNIFTY gained 303 points, or about 2.3%, and on the daily chart, it showed two interesting candles in the last two sessions—a Hanging Man on Thursday and a Spinning Top on Friday. Simply put, the index is stuck in a narrow range between 13,380 and 13,540. What’s impressive, though, is that MIDCPNIFTY closed all five sessions in green compared to the previous close, showing it was more bullish than both NIFTY and BANKNIFTY this week. SENSEX - Technical Analysis Monthly Timeframe The Sensex monthly chart shows an almost identical pattern to NIFTY, falling just 361 points short of a record-high monthly close. Sensex gained 3,671 points, or 4.57%, in October, making it one of its strongest monthly performances this year, second only to March. The broader trend remains firmly bullish, with momentum clearly intact heading into November. Weekly Timeframe The index lost 273 points, or about 0.3%, compared to last week’s close. The overall structure mirrors NIFTY and BANKNIFTY, showing consolidation after a strong run. With almost no gains over the past two weeks, Sensex has breached key support at 84,100, closing below it at 83,938. Resistance remains around 85,300, followed by the all-time high zone near 86,000, while the next support sits near 83,100. So, for now, the index looks range-bound with a mild downward bias, unless buyers step in around the 84,000 zone. Daily Timeframe Sensex is showing a pattern very similar to NIFTY, with price action mostly consolidating through the week and selling pressure in the last two sessions. Resistance remains near 85,300, which aligns with last week’s high, while support is holding around 83,100, consistent with the weekly levels. Market Metrics Summary Rate of Change For October, performance was green across all major indices. MIDCPNIFTY led the pack with a 6.89% gain, followed by BANKNIFTY at 5.75%, and SENSEX with 4.57%. Looking at the year-to-date numbers, BANK NIFTY continues to lead with an impressive +13.6%, followed by NIFTY at +8.8%. Interestingly, even after a strong October, MIDCPNIFTY still trails behind—up only about +4.34% for the year. All of those gains have actually come in the past six months, where the index is up a solid +11.53%. It’s been a late but strong comeback for the midcaps after a sluggish start to the year. Let’s see if November brings the momentum back across the board. Directional Bias Even with two weeks of no meaningful gains, the directional bias across all major indices remains positive in the short to medium term. All indices are still trading above their 21- and 50-day EMAs on the daily timeframe, indicating that the broader trend stays intact despite near-term consolidation. Sectoral Performance PSU Banks and Metals continued their strong run from last week, gaining 4.69% and 2.56%, respectively. Joining them this time were Commodities, Energy, and Infra, all posting around 2% gains each for the week—showing a broad-based recovery beyond financials. Volatility & Derivatives Range and Expiries NIFTY had its widest range day on Friday—243 points—followed by Tuesday’s 232-point move on the monthly expiry. The 5-day average range is around 200 points, roughly the same as the 10-day average, showing NIFTY has been swinging about 200 points daily for the past two weeks. BANKNIFTY, MIDCPNIFTY, and SENSEX show a similar 5-day and 10-day range structure, reflecting a phase of contained volatility. Interestingly, last Friday’s 2DTE NIFTY straddle premium was around 185 points, and this week it’s risen to 218 points—meaning the market is pricing in more volatility ahead. Let’s just hope that volatility shows up on the upside. Now, talking about the NIFTY expiry—it was typical of a monthly expiry—full of volatility. The index rallied 112 points in the first 30 minutes, then slipped 231 points till about 2:15 PM, and finally recovered 155 points in the last hour, ending the day by forming a perfect doji on the daily chart. It was the kind of session that left short-volatility sellers exhausted—classic expiry behavior. But that’s how expiries go—some play out like NIFTY, full of whipsaws, and some like SENSEX, which gave a clean, directional 600-point drop… except for the last-hour shenanigans. India VIX VIX inched up 4.65% this week to close at 12.15. Now, that’s still low—but after months of calm, it’s a sign that volatility might be mean-reverting. Is the market a little worried? Maybe. Could be earnings season, or even chatter around the US–India tariff deal—both can make traders hedge a bit more. But at these levels, it’s less about fear and more about the market saying, “Alright, things have been too quiet for too long—time for some action.” Commodities Update (Data: MCX Continuous Futures - Back Adjusted) After a strong October, Gold cooled off slightly, slipping 0.87% for the week, while Silver managed a modest 1.64% gain. Both, however, remain firmly positive for the month and year, with Gold up 4.16% MTD and 51% YTD, and Silver up 5.23% MTD and 61% YTD—easily outperforming equities in 2025. Copper added 0.98% this week, extending its steady uptrend, while Crude Oil stayed almost flat, down just 0.04%, and Natural Gas stole the spotlight, surging 11.33% for the week. So overall, metals continue to shine, energy is mixed, and natural gas leads the pack. Weekly Market Wrap The market teased us again this week. After an impressive October rally, it looked like NIFTY might march toward a new all-time high—but it ran out of steam right at the finish line. Despite a strong start, the index couldn’t hold on to its mid-week gains and slipped back into its familiar 26,100–25,700 range. BANKNIFTY and MIDCPNIFTY, though, still look relatively stronger, both closing October at record monthly highs. The broader structure across indices continues to suggest consolidation rather than reversal—a pause, not a pullback. Sectors like PSU Banks, Metals, and Energy extended their leadership, while IT and FMCG cooled off. Volatility, measured by India VIX, ticked higher to 12.15, hinting that the calm of recent months might be ending. Gold and Silver took a breather after a stellar run, while Natural Gas and Copper continued to shine. So far, it’s been a textbook healthy pause within a broader uptrend. The key question now—will the market bounce from this base or break lower from here? What to Expect Next Week Next week looks relatively quiet on the event front—no major data or policy announcements are lined up. That means markets may take their cues from global developments and stock-specific earnings instead. Still, keep an eye on the US–India tariff deal chatter—any progress there could act as the next spark. And on a lighter note, it’s also the ICC Women’s World Cup 2025 Final—India vs. South Africa—on Sunday, November 2. So expect some excitement off the trading screens too. Let’s see if the markets get inspired by our Women’s World Cup team and carry that winning energy into the new month. Until then—stay curious, stay steady, and have a great weekend! That’s pretty much this week. And yes—don’t forget to subscribe to this channel. See you soon!

text: Hello Zerodha Team, I recently discovered that Coin does not support eMandates, NACH mandates, or UPI AutoPay for NRE accounts. This was quite surprising, especially since your platform prominently states that mutual fund investments are supported for NRI customers. This defeats one of the primary benefits of SIP investing—automation and disciplined investing without the need for monthly action. To rule out any banking limitations, I checked with my bank and confirmed that they support eMandates, NACH, and UPI mandates for NRE accounts. context: Product updates over the last year at Zerodha
text: Here is the list of all the tech updates. Many are behind the scenes to improve the platform’s speed, efficiency and reliability. Kite Instant Sell and Unpledge: We now enable clients to instantly sell securities that are pledged for collateral margin. This spares our customers the extra day usually needed to unpledge securities, particularly valuable during market volatility. We are closing working to allow instant pledge of free securities in your account for collateral margin too. Order Tagging on Kite: Previously available only on Console for post-trade implementation, you can now tag your orders directly in the order window to ensure nothing slips through the cracks. Auction Orders: We are the only retail broker in India that allows placing orders in the auction market. In auction markets, the exchange invites sellers to offer their shares that are short-delivered. Stocks often trade at higher prices in these settings. Government Securities on Kite: We’ve transitioned the placement of bids on government securities from Coin to Kite, allowing our users to execute both primary and secondary market trades on a single platform. Virtual Contract Note: This feature provides an estimated breakdown of brokerage, STT, stamp duty, exchange transaction charges, SEBI turnover charges, and GST for the day. Unlike traditional contract notes, this version also offers order-wise charge details. Trading in BSE Index Derivatives: We have introduced trading in Sensex F&O contracts. ChartIQ Charting Upgrade: Our charting library has been updated to the latest version of ChartIQ, a change that had been pending for over three years. In the next quarter, we will also update our TradingView library to the latest version. While those updates focus on the front-end experience, our tech team has been diligently working on backend improvements to ensure a faster, more reliable platform: In-house OMS/RMS: Our in-house R&D OMS/RMS project that has been running for 3+ years is now in internal beta. This makes us one of the few brokers with an in-house OMS/RMS, and perhaps the one to have built one afresh in the last decade. As always, we have continued to make significant and massive infrastructural upgrades and improvements for scale and stability to all our systems. Many of these are specifically with a view on scaling smoothly into the next decade. Pre-application for IPOs: Users can now pre-apply for IPOs before the bid opening date. Console- our backoffice & reporting tool Family account - In Console, you can now add your family members having Zerodha demat account to your Console’s family account and view the consolidated holdings and respective analytics. Verified P&L - We introduced Verified P&L allowing users to publicly share their Console P&L report by sharing a link, ensuring its authenticity. It addresses two concerns: genuine traders can enhance their credibility in the market, while consumers can depend on factual data, resulting in improved confidence in the stock market. Backend database migration of our tradebooks and ledgers- Our developers found that the existing DB isn’t scalable enough. Hence, we’ve been migrating every process to a new DB, which helps us scale further and reduces the time to complete daily processes for improved efficiency. Payin & Payout of securities - Across the industry, the DP process primarily depends on vendors, which comes with limitations and is slow to change. To keep up with the phase at which regulations are being amended and to launch new features quickly, we’ve started doing DP process in-house. Standardisation of file formats - Both BSE and NSE updated the daily end of day files like Bhavcopy, scrip master, trade file, position files etc which are required to do the daily trade and P&L process to deduct the proper obligation and charges and for accurate reporting i.e P&L. context: ETFs VS Index Fund: Where Should Investor Invest?
text: ETFs and index Funds are two of the popular forms of passive investing. ETFs can also be actively managed, but for the sake of comparison, we will only consider passive investments. The advantage of passive investing is the simplicity it offers, such that you do not have to choose from the plethora of investment options. These simply mirror the holdings/ weightage of an index or an exchange. This article will give you an insight into how do these two differ in terms of expense ratio, flexibility, or liquidity and where should investor invest? An index fund is a passive mutual fund that aims to achieve capital appreciation by imitating or replicating an index, such as the Sensex or Nifty. The objective of an index fund or an index ETF is to passively replicate or mirror the index in terms of its portfolio composition. For instance, if the S&P BSE SENSEX contains 11% of HDFC shares then the index fund will also contain the same proportion of HDFC shares. ETFs (Exchange Traded Funds) comprise shares that follow an index such as NSE Nifty 50 or BSE Sensex. As the name suggests, ETFs can be bought and sold on the stock exchanges. There are some new generation index ETFs based on popular sectors such as S&P BSE Auto, or FMCG, banking and healthcare. Let’s understand the parameters where ETF and index fund differs: Timing the Market Investing in ETFs can be an advantage if you can take the opportunity of the price movements that occur during the day based on your analysis of the market or the index. In contrast, Index funds are suitable to those who do not require extensive tracking and anticipate performance that is in line with the market returns. Flexibility ETFs are considered more flexible than most index funds. ETFs can be traded on exchanges intra-day, like common stocks. You can buy ETFs at your convenience. You can buy Mutual funds units by placing a request with the fund house either online or through RIA or through a distributor. Liquidity You can trade ETFs more easily than index funds as they can be redeemed or sold anytime during market hours. Their market price is available in real-time just like common stocks. An index fund, on the other hand, can be redeemed only at the end of the day’s NAV (Net Asset Value). NAV indicates the price per unit of a mutual fund. Ease of investing Index funds are a good option for a first-time investor or if you are looking for ease of investing because you do not need to research. Index Funds also offer you the option of investing through an SIP (systematic investment plan). This gives the added benefit of compounding your mutual fund returns with time and rupee-cost averaging which allows you to average out your cost of investment. They also offer the benefit of STPs (Systematic Transfer Plan) or SWPs (Systematic Withdrawal Plan). However, index funds come with a tracking error. Index Funds tracking error indicates how much the fund performance has deviated from the benchmark index. Tracking error occurs in both scenarios; i.e. outperforming the index and underperforming the index. Since ETFs trade like a stock, you can easily refer to the price change using the ticker symbol and compare it with the benchmark or commodity. Professional Fund Management A fund manager of an index fund keeps track of any changes in the weightage of stocks. He /she creates a portfolio that mirrors the index performance as closely as possible. Tracking error occurs in both scenarios; i.e. outperforming the index and underperforming the index. Since ETFs track an index or a commodity, it does not need professional fund management. Expense Ratio & other charges If you are investing in an ETF, you may need to incur the DEMAT account’s annual maintenance charges and transaction charges with a marginal expense ratio. Index funds come with a relatively higher expense ratio and exit loads in case you withdraw the mutual fund units before a particular timeframe. DEMAT Account IF you want to invest in ETFs, you need a DEMAT account. However, when investing in index mutual funds, you need not have a DEMAT Account. Choosing between index funds and ETFs depends on your preferred investing style, goal and risk profile. ETFs may offer relatively lower expense ratios and greater flexibility, while index funds simplify the decisions an investor has to make. On the other hand, if you are trying to take advantage of the opportunities of the market movements, you can consider investing in ETFs. Not every ETF/ index fund may be suited to your goals. When investing in sector-specific funds, you need to take into consideration that these funds address a limited universe. As an investor, you might choose to invest in an index mutual fund and add ETFs that invest in assets or sectors to diversify your mutual fund portfolio. Both index funds and ETFs are good for long-term investing. context: Regular vs Direct Plan in MFs
text: Hi Shivam, NAV of a scheme is derived from the summation of several factors or variables which is known as the profitability metric. It consists of the following variables : (1) Interest income (2) + Dividend income (3) + Realized capital gains (4) + Valuation gains (5) – Realized capital losses (6) – Valuation losses (7) – Scheme expenses As you can see the 7th variable which is the scheme expenses is a subtraction so basically the NAV would be lesser if this is higher. The expense ration is nothing but the scheme expenses. The expense ratio is generally denoted as a percentage which is specified as per annum. For the calculation of the NAV, the scheme expense is calculated and deducted on daily basis. Now, for a regular plan of a particular mutual fund scheme the expense ratio is higher than that of a direct plan of the same scheme which means that the scheme expenses is higher for a regular plan. Thus, the NAV of a direct plan will always be higher than that of a regular plan. This means that the returns generated for a direct plan is essentially much higher than that of a regular plan. Below is a graph which shows the difference in the NAVs of a direct plan and regular plan of L&T India Emerging Business Fund. The NAV shown in the figure for a particular month is the average value of daily NAVs released for that particular month. The orange line represents the NAV of direct plan and the blue line represents the NAV of a regular plan. You can observe that the lines are slightly overlapping each other from the month of January 2015 and there is a huge divergence in the month September 2017. This is because the AMC had gradually revised the expense ratio of regular plan and the difference in the NAVs of direct and regular plans became more significant. image 1031×570 105 KB So, investing in the direct plan of this fund would have yielded you more returns than investing in a regular plan of the same.

context: SWPs for mutual funds investments are now live on Coin
text: Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) on Coin for your Mutual Funds Investments is now live. Zerodha SWPs, distinct from conventional SWPs provided by Asset Management Companies, and allows users to systematically withdraw funds from the mutual fund holdings, set the frequency as per the requirement and pause it whenever required. How Zerodha SWP works? Zerodha SWP operates based on the selected withdrawal amount, with unit calculations made on the execution date. You can set up an SWP with a minimum amount of ₹500, and choose from various withdrawal frequencies such as weekly, fortnightly, monthly, and quarterly. SWP requests can be initiated one day before the trigger date. Orders are automatically triggered on the chosen date at 10:00 AM and are processed by 3:00 PM on the same business day. On the specified order trigger date, our backend system calculates the units based on the Net Asset Value (NAV) from the previous trading day (T-1 day) and places a redemption order directly with the exchange. Please note that once an order is triggered, it cannot be cancelled. How does Zerodha SWP order execution work for Non-POA and Non-DDPI users? For users without Power of Attorney (POA) or Demat Debt Instruction (DDPI), the user must authorize the units through CDSL before 3:00 PM on the same day. You will receive a notification from the Coin app and an email as well to authorize the units on the same day otherwise the order will fail. To learn more, see How can units be authorized for redemption on CDSL after a SWP order is triggered? How to create a SWP? To create a SWP, follow these steps: Tap on Investments. Select the fund from the portfolio section and tap on it. Tap on 3 dots and tap on SWP. Enter the withdrawal amount. Select the frequency. Tap on Create SWP. To learn more, see What is SWP and how to create one on Coin app? Anything else you need to understand about SWP SWPs can be created one day prior to the desired withdrawal date. SWPs can be created for ELSS (Equity Linked Saving Scheme) schemes, and there are no restrictions on creating SWP requests for units in a lock-in period. On non-business days, SWP orders will be triggered but processed on the next working day. The number of units redeemed for SWP is determined based on the NAV of the previous trading day (T-1) using the formula: Redemption Units = SWP Amount / T-1 Day's NAV If all units for a particular scheme are redeemed, the SWP order will fail, and a notification will be triggered. SWP orders will have a distinct tag in the order history for easy identification.

Calculate how many whole units fit within the user’s defined ‘Fixed Amount.’ Execute the order for that calculated quantity and leave the small remaining balance in the Kite ledger. This would bring the ‘set-and-forget’ convenience of Coin (Mutual Funds) to the cost-effective world of ETFs on Kite. It would be a game-changer for disciplined, minimalist investors who prefer ETFs for their lower expense ratios and transparency. Looking forward to seeing this in a future update! #kite #feedback

text: I think you need to understand a couple of things here. All these top company CEOs are saying good things about Indiamarket. just because they have to exit their investments at a good valuation. Imagine if they started pointing out the real issues: they would not be able to pull their investments out at a good profit. So, they say good things, and when the time is right, they just start exiting (which is already what FIIs are doing currently). Now, there are two main things working against investing in India: 1. Rupee depreciation: for an FII, you do not invest in dollars, you invest in rupees. If the rupee is depreciating 5-7% per year, you have to factor that into your actual returns. If you are making an average of 8% long-term, but currency depreciation eats up 7%, your net return can even end up negative. Because of that, it makes very little sense for someone outside India to invest in the Indian market. 2. Long-term capital gains tax: it is currently and that also works directly against returns. So, I really do not think you should take every public comment optimistically.
